subject: Assistance with DSM Data Formatting for Curved Transects

messages.author: 9b66de3535c8ae0a
messages.subject: Assistance with DSM Data Formatting for Curved Transects
parts:
Hi,

I hope this is the right place to reach out with a question about Density Surface Models. If not, would you be able to direct me to someone who might be able to help?

My question concerns the segmentation of transects using the function segs <- st_segmentize(transects, dfMaxLength=units::set_units(2000, "metres")). Unlike the example found here `dsm` data formatting example , my transects are not straight lines due to the complex area we surveyed in the northern GBRMP. This function is producing very short segments, which may affect subsequent analysis by resulting in an excess of small segments and a large number of rows linking to observations.
We suspect this may be due to the curved nature of our transects. When I manually adjust the transects to be straighter, the segment lengths approach the truncation distance (doubled) more closely. However, this might bias the sample.

Should I continuing with the actual curved transects despite the small segments, or might another function yield more uniform segment lengths? Alternatively, could I use GIS software for segmentation be a viable solution, or is there a different approach for these type of transects?

Thank you for taking the time to consider my questions.

Valeria

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Assistance with DSM Data Formatting for Curved Transects
parts:
Valeria

The case study web page to which you point is one example of automatic code segmentation. I believe the code was intended to be used with transects that are approximately straight. As is indicated in the web page
If you are fluent in ArcGIS or QGIS I recommend doing this task in the software you are familiar with at first. A simple guide to doing this task in QGIS is here and for ArcGIS I recommend the MGET toolbox.
"st_segmentize" is not always the right tool for the job, as in your case.
